questions.stem: What makes a playbook appear for a Security Incident if using Flow Designer?

options.text: Trigger set to conditions that match the security incident

questions.explanation: A playbook appears for a Security Incident in Flow Designer when the Trigger is set to conditions that match the security incident. The Flow's trigger conditions determine when it executes — if those conditions match the current security incident's attributes (e.g., category, priority), the playbook becomes available. Actions, Runbook properties, and Service Criticality do not control playbook visibility.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of Calculator Groups as opposed to Calculators?

options.text: To provide metadata about the calculators
To allow the agent to select which calculator they want to execute
To set the condition for all calculators to run
To ensure one at maximum will run per group

questions.explanation: Calculator Groups ensure that at most one calculator will run per group. When multiple calculators exist within a group, only the first matching calculator executes. This prevents conflicting calculations from running simultaneously. Calculators within a group are evaluated in order, and once one matches, the remaining calculators in that group are skipped.

questions.stem: The following term is used to describe any observable occurrence: __________.
questions.explanation: An Event is the term used to describe any observable occurrence. In security and IT operations, an event is any detectable or discernible occurrence that has significance for the management of infrastructure or delivery of services. Events may be informational, warning, or exception-level. Incidents, logs, tickets, and alerts are derived from or created in response to events.

questions.stem: The severity field of the security incident is influenced by what?

options.text: The cost of the response to the security breach
The impact, urgency and priority of the incident
The time taken to resolve the security incident
The business value of the affected asset

questions.explanation: The severity field of a security incident is influenced by the business value of the affected asset. Security Incident Response uses calculators that factor in the business criticality and value of affected CIs and Business Services to determine severity. Higher-value assets result in higher severity ratings. Cost of response, time to resolve, and impact/urgency/priority are separate considerations.

questions.stem: The Risk Score is calculated by combining all the weights using __________.
questions.explanation: The Risk Score is calculated by combining all the weights using a geometric mean. The geometric mean multiplies all weighted values together and takes the nth root, which prevents any single factor from disproportionately affecting the score. This is more appropriate than arithmetic mean for combining diverse risk factors with different scales and weights.

questions.stem: What are two of the audiences identified that will need reports and insight into Security Incident Response reports? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Two key audiences for Security Incident Response reports are Analysts (who need operational data about incidents they're working) and Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) (who needs executive-level security posture and trend reporting). Vulnerability Managers work with VR, not SIR directly. Problem Managers handle ITSM problems, not security incident reporting.

questions.stem: What three steps enable you to include a new playbook in the Selected Playbook choice list? (Choose three.)

options.text: Add the TLP: GREEN tag to the playbooks that you want to include in the Selected Playbook choice list
Search for the new playbook you have created using Flow Designer
Add the sir_playbook tag to the playbooks that you want to include in the Selected Playbook choice list

questions.explanation: To include a new playbook in the Selected Playbook choice list: Navigate to the sys_hub_flow.list table (B) to find your flows, Search for the new playbook created using Flow Designer (C), and Add the sir_playbook tag to the playbooks you want to include (D). The sir_playbook tag marks a flow as available in the Selected Playbook dropdown. TLP:GREEN is a security classification tag, not a playbook inclusion tag.

questions.stem: Which improvement opportunity can be found baseline which can contribute towards process maturity and strengthen costumer’s overall security posture?
questions.explanation: Post-Incident Review is the improvement opportunity found baseline that contributes towards process maturity and strengthens the customer's overall security posture. Post-Incident Reviews analyze what happened, what went well, what could be improved, and document lessons learned. This continuous improvement cycle is fundamental to maturing security incident response processes.

questions.stem: What is the fastest way for security incident administrators to remove unwanted widgets from the Security Incident Catalog?

options.text: Clicking the X on the top right corner

questions.explanation: The fastest way for security incident administrators to remove unwanted widgets from the Security Incident Catalog is through the Catalog Definition record. Catalog items are managed through their definition records where administrators can activate, deactivate, or modify them. The X button and system administrator involvement are not the recommended approaches.

questions.stem: Select the one capability that retrieves a list of running processes on a CI from a host or endpoint.
questions.explanation: Get Running Processes is the capability that retrieves a list of running processes on a CI from a host or endpoint. This integration action queries the endpoint and returns process information for investigation. Get Network Statistics retrieves connection data, Isolate Host restricts connectivity, Block Action prevents access, Sightings Search looks for observables, and Publish Watchlist shares indicators.

questions.stem: Which Table would be commonly used for Security Incident Response?
questions.explanation: The sn_si_incident table is commonly used for Security Incident Response. This is the main table storing security incident records in the SIR scoped application (sn_si prefix). The sysapproval_approver table handles approvals, cmdb_rel_ci stores CI relationships, and sec_ops_incident is not the correct table name for SIR.

questions.stem: There are several methods in which security incidents can be raised, which broadly fit into one of these categories: __________. (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Security incidents can be raised through methods that broadly fit into two categories: Manually created (analysts or users create incidents through forms, catalogs, or UI actions) and Automatically created (through integrations, event processing, email parsing, or automated rules). Integrations and Email parsing are specific methods within these broad categories, not categories themselves.

questions.stem: What is the first step when creating a security Playbook?
questions.explanation: The first step when creating a security Playbook is to Create a Flow. In Flow Designer, you start by creating a flow that defines the trigger conditions and the sequence of actions. Once the flow exists, you add response task creation actions, configure knowledge articles for runbooks, and set task states. The flow is the container for all playbook logic.

questions.stem: To configure Security Incident Escalations, you need the following role(s): __________.
questions.explanation: To configure Security Incident Escalations, you need the sn_si.admin role. The SIR admin role has full configuration access to all Security Incident Response settings, including escalation rules and configurations. The sn_si.manager role manages incidents operationally but does not have configuration privileges for escalation setup.

questions.stem: Which of the following are potential benefits for utilizing Security Incident assignment automation? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Benefits of utilizing Security Incident assignment automation include Decreased Time to Containment (faster assignment means faster response and containment) and Increased resolution process consistency (automated assignment follows defined rules consistently). Increased Mean Time to Remediation would be negative (you want decreased MTTR). Decreased Time to Ingestion relates to data collection, not assignment.

questions.stem: What is the key to a successful implementation?

options.text: Sell customer the most expensive package
Understanding the customer’s goals and objectives

questions.explanation: The key to a successful implementation is understanding the customer's goals and objectives. Without clear understanding of what the customer wants to achieve, any implementation risks missing the mark. Selling expensive packages, implementing everything, and building custom integrations are not success factors — alignment with customer goals is paramount.

questions.stem: A flow consists of one or more actions and a what?
questions.explanation: A flow consists of one or more actions and a Trigger. The trigger defines the condition that initiates the flow (e.g., record created, record updated, schedule). Actions are the steps the flow executes. Together, the trigger and actions form the complete flow. Change formatter, Catalog Designer, and NIST Ready State are unrelated to flow components.

questions.stem: Flow Triggers can be based on what? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Flow Triggers can be based on Record changes (when a record field is modified), Schedules (time-based triggers), and Record inserts (when a new record is created). These are the three standard trigger types in Flow Designer. Subflows are reusable flow components, not triggers, and Record views do not trigger flows.

questions.stem: Which one of the following users is automatically added to the Request Assessments list?

options.text: Any user that adds a worknote to the ticket
The analyst assigned to the ticket
Any user who has Response Tasks on the incident
The Affected User on the incident

questions.explanation: The analyst assigned to the ticket is automatically added to the Request Assessments list. When a security incident is assigned, the assigned analyst is included as an assessor for post-incident review questionnaires. Users who add worknotes, users with response tasks, and affected users are not automatically added to the assessment list.

questions.stem: For Customers who don't use 3rd-party systems, what ways can security incidents be created? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: For customers without third-party systems, security incidents can be created through: Security Service Catalog (user-facing request forms), Security Incident Form (direct record creation by analysts), and Inbound Email Parsing Rules (email-based incident creation). Leveraging an Integration requires third-party systems, and Alert Management is an integration-dependent feature.

questions.stem: What does a flow require?
questions.explanation: A flow requires a Trigger. Every flow must have a trigger that defines when and under what conditions the flow executes. Without a trigger, a flow cannot be initiated. Security orchestration flows, Runbooks, and CAB orders are not requirements for a flow — they are separate concepts.

questions.stem: Knowledge articles that describe steps an analyst needs to follow to complete Security incident tasks might be associated to those tasks through which of the following?
questions.explanation: Knowledge articles describing steps an analyst needs to follow are associated to Security Incident tasks through a Runbook. Runbooks link knowledge articles to response tasks, providing step-by-step guidance. When a response task references a runbook, the analyst can access the associated knowledge article for instructions. Flows, Workflows, and Flow Designer are automation tools, not content links.

questions.stem: Which of the following process definitions allow only single-step progress through the process defined without allowing step skipping?
questions.explanation: NIST Stateful and SANS Stateful process definitions allow only single-step progress through the process without allowing step skipping. Stateful processes enforce sequential progression — an incident must move through each state in order. Open process definitions (NIST Open and SANS Open) allow flexible, non-sequential state transitions where steps can be skipped.

questions.stem: If the customer’s email server currently has an account setup to report suspicious emails, then what happens next?

options.text: an integration added to Exchange keeps the ServiceNow platform in sync
the ServiceNow platform ensures that parsing and analysis takes place on their mail server
the customer’s systems are already handling suspicious emails
the customer should set up a rule to forward these mails onto the ServiceNow platform

questions.explanation: If the customer's email server already has an account set up for reporting suspicious emails, the customer should set up a rule to forward these emails to the ServiceNow platform. This allows ServiceNow's inbound email processing to parse the forwarded phishing emails and create security incidents. The existing email account continues receiving reports while ServiceNow handles the analysis.

questions.stem: What parts of the Security Incident Response lifecycle is responsible for limiting the impact of a security incident?
questions.explanation: Containment, Eradication, and Recovery is the phase responsible for limiting the impact of a security incident. Containment stops the spread, Eradication removes the threat, and Recovery restores systems to normal operation. This is the third phase of the NIST incident response lifecycle, following Preparation and Detection & Analysis.

questions.stem: Select the one capability that restricts connections from one CI to other devices.
questions.explanation: Isolate Host is the capability that restricts connections from one CI to other devices. This integration action quarantines an endpoint by limiting its network connectivity, preventing lateral movement of threats. Block Action prevents specific traffic, Get Running Processes retrieves process lists, Get Network Statistics shows connections, and Publish Watchlist shares indicators.

questions.stem: What factor, if any, limits the ability to close SIR records?

options.text: Best practice dictates that SIR records should be set to 'Resolved' never to 'Closed'
Nothing, SIR records could be closed at any time
All post-incident review questioners have to be completed first

questions.explanation: Nothing limits the ability to close SIR records — they can be closed at any time. Security incidents do not have a mandatory prerequisite for closure in the baseline configuration. While best practices suggest completing post-incident reviews, the system does not enforce this. Open related incidents do not block SIR closure, and there is no mandatory questionnaire completion requirement.

questions.stem: When the Security Phishing Email record is created what types of observables are stored in the record? (Choose three.)

options.text: URLs, domains, or IP addresses appearing in the body
Hashes and/or file names found in the EML attachment
Type of Ingestion Rule used to identify this email as a phishing attempt

questions.explanation: When a Security Phishing Email record is created, the following observable types are stored: URLs, domains, or IP addresses appearing in the body (A), IP addresses from the header (D), and Hashes and/or file names found in the EML attachment (E). These are the technical indicators extracted from the phishing email. Who reported it, state, and ingestion rule type are metadata, not observables.

questions.stem: What plugin must be activated to see the New Security Analyst UI?
questions.explanation: The Security Operations UI plugin must be activated to see the New Security Analyst UI. This plugin provides the updated workspace interface for security analysts working with Security Operations applications including SIR. The Security Analyst UI Plugin, SIR UI plugin, and Security Agent UI Plugin are not the correct plugin names.

questions.stem: The benefits of improved Security Incident Response are expressed __________.

options.text: as desirable outcomes with clear, measurable Key Performance Indicators
differently depending upon 3 stages: Process Improvement, Process Design, and Post Go-Live
as a series of states with consistent, clear metrics
as a value on a scale of 1-10 based on specific outcomes

questions.explanation: The benefits of improved Security Incident Response are expressed as desirable outcomes with clear, measurable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Metrics like Mean Time to Contain (MTTC), Mean Time to Remediation (MTTR), and incident volume trends provide quantifiable measures of SIR effectiveness. This allows organizations to track improvement over time.

questions.stem: This type of integration workflow helps retrieve a list of active network connections from a host or endpoint, so it can be used to enrich incidents during investigation.

options.text: Security Incident Response – Get Running Services
Security Incident Response – Get Network Statistics

questions.explanation: Security Incident Response - Get Network Statistics is the integration workflow that retrieves a list of active network connections from a host or endpoint for incident enrichment during investigation. Get Running Services retrieves service lists, Sightings Search checks for observable matches, and Block Request prevents access — none retrieve active network connections.

questions.stem:
Joe is on the SIR Team and needs to be able to configure Territories and Skills.
What role does he need?
questions.explanation: Joe needs the Security Admin (sn_si.admin) role to configure Territories and Skills in Security Incident Response. Configuration of assignment-related settings like territories and skills requires administrative privileges. Security Basic (sn_si.basic) and Security Analyst (sn_si.analyst) roles lack configuration access, and Manager (sn_si.manager) manages incident workflow, not system configuration.

questions.stem: Why should discussions focus with the end in mind?
questions.explanation: Discussions should focus with the end in mind to understand desired outcomes. Starting with the customer's desired end state ensures implementation efforts align with their goals. Understanding how they define success guides decisions about process design, automation priorities, and configuration choices throughout the project.

questions.stem: Which of the following State Flows are provided for Security Incidents? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Security Incidents provide three State Flows: NIST Open (flexible NIST-based states), SANS Open (flexible SANS-based states), and SANS Stateful (sequential SANS-based states). NIST Stateful also exists as a fourth option but the question asks for three. NIST Open, SANS Open, and SANS Stateful are the three most commonly referenced baseline state flows.

questions.stem: Chief factors when configuring auto-assignment of Security Incidents are __________.

options.text: Agent group membership, Agent location and time zone
Security incident priority, CI Location and agent time zone
Agent skills, System Schedules and agent location
Agent location, Agent skills and agent time zone

questions.explanation: Chief factors when configuring auto-assignment of Security Incidents are Agent location, Agent skills, and agent time zone. Auto-assignment considers which agents have the right skills for the incident type, where they are located relative to the incident, and whether they are currently working based on their time zone. Group membership and CI Location are secondary factors.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow automation capability extends Flow Designer to integrate business processes with other systems?
questions.explanation: Integration Hub is the ServiceNow automation capability that extends Flow Designer to integrate business processes with other systems. Integration Hub provides spokes (pre-built connector packages) and actions for connecting to third-party tools like SIEM, endpoint protection, and threat intelligence platforms. Workflow is legacy, Orchestration is older automation, and Subflows are reusable flow components.

questions.stem: In order to see the Actions in Flow Designer for Security Incident, what plugin must be activated?

options.text: Performance Analytics for Security Incident Response

questions.explanation: The Security Operations Spoke plugin must be activated to see the Actions in Flow Designer for Security Incident. This spoke contains pre-built flow actions specific to Security Operations, including actions for creating response tasks, enriching incidents, and integrating with security tools. The spoke name uses 'Security Operations' rather than 'Security Incident' or 'Security' alone.

questions.stem: How do you select which process definition to use?

options.text: By selecting the desired process within the Process Definition module
By selecting the desired process within the Process Selection module
By setting the process definition record to Active
By setting the Script Include record to Active

questions.explanation: You select which process definition to use by setting the process definition record to Active. Only one process definition can be active at a time for security incidents. When you activate a process definition (NIST Open, SANS Stateful, etc.), it becomes the governing state flow for all security incidents. Process Definition module and Process Selection module are not separate configuration points.

questions.stem: What role(s) are required to add new items to the Security Incident Catalog?

options.text: requires both sn_si.write and catalog_admin roles

questions.explanation: The admin (platform administrator) role is required to add new items to the Security Incident Catalog. Catalog item creation requires platform-level catalog administration permissions. The sn_si.admin role manages SIR configuration but catalog item creation specifically requires the platform admin role. sn_si.catalog and sn_si.write are not standard SIR roles.

questions.stem: What is calculated as an arithmetic mean taking into consideration different values in the CI, Security Incident, and User records?
questions.explanation: The Risk Score is calculated as an arithmetic mean (actually geometric mean per Q5, but this question specifically asks what uses arithmetic mean considering CI, Security Incident, and User records). Risk Score combines weighted values from CI business criticality, Security Incident attributes, and User information. Priority, Business Impact, and Severity are individual fields, not composite calculations using all three record types.

questions.stem: What is the name of the Inbound Action that validates whether an inbound email should be processed as a phishing email for URP v2?
questions.explanation: User Reporting Phishing (for Forwarded emails) is the Inbound Action that validates whether an inbound email should be processed as a phishing email for URP v2. This action processes forwarded suspicious emails, checking headers and content to determine if they qualify as phishing reports. The 'for Forwarded emails' variant handles the common case where users forward suspicious emails to a reporting mailbox.

questions.stem: When a record is created in the Security Incident Phishing Email table what is triggered to create a Security Incident?
questions.explanation: When a record is created in the Security Incident Phishing Email table, an Ingestion Rule is triggered to create a Security Incident. Ingestion rules evaluate phishing email records and determine whether to create a security incident, what priority to assign, and how to classify it. Transform flows/workflows and Duplication Rules serve different purposes in the SIR pipeline.

questions.stem: If a desired pre-built integration cannot be found in the platform, what should be your next step to find a certified integration?

options.text: Build your own through the REST API Explorer
Ask for assistance in the community page
Look for one in the ServiceNow Store

questions.explanation: If a desired pre-built integration cannot be found in the platform, the next step is to look for one in the ServiceNow Store. The ServiceNow Store is the official marketplace for certified integrations, applications, and plugins built by ServiceNow and partners. ServiceNow Share hosts community-contributed content that is not certified. Building custom integrations should be a last resort.

questions.stem:
Incident severity is influenced by the business value of the affected asset.
Which of the following are asset types that can be affected by an incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Asset types that can be affected by a security incident and influence severity include Business Service (representing critical business functions) and Configuration Item (representing IT infrastructure components). Calculator Groups and Severity Calculators are SIR calculation mechanisms, not asset types. The business value of these assets directly impacts incident severity scoring.

questions.stem: A pre-planned response process contains which sequence of events?
questions.explanation: A pre-planned response process contains the sequence: Organize, Verify, Prioritize, Contain. This sequence ensures that when an incident occurs, the team first organizes their response, verifies the incident is real, prioritizes based on impact, and then takes containment actions. This structured approach prevents premature containment of false positives.

questions.stem: Why is it important that the Platform (System) Administrator and the Security Incident administrator role be separated? (Choose three.)

options.text: Access to security incident data may need to be restricted
Allow SIR Teams to control assignment of security roles
Reduce the number of incidents assigned to the Platform Admin
Preserve the security image in the company

questions.explanation: The Platform Administrator and SIR administrator roles should be separated for three reasons: Access to security incident data may need to be restricted (A) since security incidents contain sensitive information, Allow SIR Teams to control assignment of security roles (B) maintaining independence, and Clear separation of duty (C) which is a fundamental security principle. Reducing incident assignment and preserving image are not primary reasons.

questions.stem: Using the KB articles for Playbooks tasks also gives you which of these advantages?

options.text: Automated activities to run scans and enrich Security Incidents with real time data
Automated activities to resolve security Incidents through patching
Improved visibility to threats and vulnerabilities
Enhanced ability to create and present concise, descriptive tasks

questions.explanation: Using Knowledge Base articles for Playbook tasks gives you an enhanced ability to create and present concise, descriptive tasks. KB articles provide structured, reusable content that clearly describes what an analyst needs to do for each task. Automated scanning, patching, and threat/vulnerability visibility are integration capabilities, not KB article benefits.

questions.stem: The EmailUserReportedPhishing script include processes inbound emails and creates a record in which table?
questions.explanation: The EmailUserReportedPhishing script include processes inbound emails and creates a record in the sn_si_phishing_email table. This table stores parsed phishing email records including headers, body content, attachments, and extracted observables. The sn_si_incident table stores security incidents (created later), and sn_si_phishing_email_header stores header details separately.

questions.stem: A flow consists of __________. (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A flow consists of Actions (the operations the flow performs) and Triggers (the conditions that initiate the flow). Every flow must have at least one trigger and one or more actions. Scripts, Processes, and Actors are not components of a Flow Designer flow. Actions define what happens, triggers define when it happens.

questions.stem: Which of the following process definitions are not provided baseline?
questions.explanation: SAN Stateful (note: 'SAN' not 'SANS') is not provided baseline. The baseline process definitions are NIST Open, NIST Stateful, SANS Open, and SANS Stateful. 'SAN Stateful' is a misspelling/variation that does not exist as a standard process definition. The question tests attention to the exact naming of provided process definitions.

questions.stem: Which of the following tag classifications are provided baseline? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Baseline tag classifications in SIR include Traffic Light Protocol (TLP tags like RED, AMBER, GREEN, WHITE for information sharing), Severity (classification by incident severity), and Cyber Kill Chain Step (categorizing observables by attack phase). Block from Sharing, IoC Type, Escalation Level, and Enrichment whitelist/blacklist are not baseline tag classifications.

questions.stem:
David is on the Network team and has been assigned a security incident response task.
What role does he need to be able to view and work the task?
questions.explanation: David needs the Security Basic (sn_si.basic) role to view and work security incident response tasks. The sn_si.basic role allows users to view and update security incidents, tasks, and related records without full analyst capabilities. Security Analyst provides more privileges than needed for task work, and External and Read roles have insufficient permissions.

questions.stem: When a service desk agent uses the Create Security Incident UI action from a regular incident, what occurs?

options.text: The incident is marked resolved with an automatic security resolution code
A security incident is raised on their behalf but only a notification is displayed
A security incident is raised on their behalf and displayed to the service desk agent
The service desk agent is redirected to the Security Incident Catalog to complete the record producer

questions.explanation: When a service desk agent uses the Create Security Incident UI action from a regular incident, a security incident is raised on their behalf and displayed to the service desk agent. The UI action creates the security incident record with pre-populated fields from the original incident and opens it for the agent to review. The agent is not redirected to a catalog, and the incident is not auto-resolved.

questions.stem: Which of the following fields is used to identify an Event that is to be used for Security purposes?
questions.explanation: The Security field (classification) is used to identify an Event that is to be used for Security purposes. When an event record has its classification set to 'Security', it is flagged for processing by Security Incident Response rather than standard IT event management. The IT classification marks standard IT events, and CI identifies the affected configuration item.

questions.stem: What field is used to distinguish Security events from other IT events?
questions.explanation: The Classification field on the em_event table is used to distinguish Security events from other IT events. When an event has a security-related classification value, it is processed by Security Incident Response instead of regular Event Management. The Type field categorizes event severity, Source identifies where the event came from, and Description contains free-text detail. Only Classification specifically flags an event as security-relevant, enabling SIR to ingest and process it into security incidents.

questions.stem: What specific role is required in order to use the REST API Explorer?
questions.explanation: The admin role is required to use the REST API Explorer. The REST API Explorer is a platform tool that requires full administrative access since it can query and modify any table. The sn_si.admin role is scoped to SIR only, rest_api_explorer is not a real role, and security_admin is not the correct role name for this purpose.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an action provided by the Security Incident Response application?

options.text: Create Record on Security Incident state V1
Create Response Task set Incident state V1
Look Up Record on Security Incident state V1

questions.explanation: Create Response Task set Incident state V1 is an action provided by the Security Incident Response application. This Flow Designer action creates a response task and optionally sets the security incident to a specific state in the process flow. The other options (Create Outage state, Create Record on SI state, Look Up Record on SI state) are not standard SIR actions.

questions.stem: Which one of the following reasons best describes why roles for Security Incident Response (SIR) begin with "sn_si"?

options.text: Because SIR is a scoped application, roles and script includes will begin with the sn_si prefix
Because the Security Incident Response application uses a Secure Identity token
Because ServiceNow checks the instance for a Secure Identity when logging on to this scoped application
Because ServiceNow tracks license use against the Security Incident Response Application

questions.explanation: SIR roles begin with 'sn_si' because SIR is a scoped application, and roles and script includes in scoped applications begin with the application scope prefix. ServiceNow scoped applications use namespace prefixes (sn_si for Security Incident) to prevent naming conflicts and maintain application isolation. This is standard ServiceNow scoped application architecture.

questions.stem: A Post Incident Review can contain which of the following? (Choose three.)

options.text: Attachments associated with the security incident

questions.explanation: A Post Incident Review can contain: Post incident questionnaires (A) for structured feedback, Attachments associated with the security incident (C) for evidence and documentation, and Key incident fields (D) summarizing the incident details. An audit trail is maintained at the platform level, and Performance Analytics reports are separate from PIR content.

questions.stem: Security tag used when a piece of information requires support to be effectively acted upon, yet carries risks to privacy, reputation, or operations if shared outside of the organizations involved.
questions.explanation: TLP:AMBER is the security tag used when information requires support to be effectively acted upon but carries risks to privacy, reputation, or operations if shared outside involved organizations. TLP:AMBER means limited disclosure — recipients may share within their organization and with clients/customers who need to know. TLP:RED is most restricted, TLP:GREEN is broad community, TLP:WHITE is unrestricted.

questions.stem: Which Table would be commonly used for Security Incident Response?
questions.explanation: The sn_si_incident table is commonly used for Security Incident Response. This is the core SIR table where security incident records are stored. The 'sn_si' prefix indicates it belongs to the Security Incident scoped application. sn_si_sec_incident and sn_sir_incident are incorrect table names, and the 'incident' table is for ITSM incidents, not security incidents.

questions.stem: ServiceNow follows the basic guidelines of the NIST lifecycle. Based on the best course of action, usually guided by runbooks and established procedures, problems sought to be fixed in which phase?
questions.explanation: In the NIST lifecycle, problems are sought to be fixed in the Eradication phase. Eradication is part of the 'Containment, Eradication, and Recovery' phase where the root cause of the incident is removed and affected systems are cleaned. Detection discovers the issue, Analysis investigates it, and Review happens post-incident.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the Security Incident Response Team?
questions.explanation: The main purpose of the Security Incident Response Team is to handle security incidents. The SIR team's core mission is to detect, analyze, contain, eradicate, and recover from security incidents. Managing vulnerability response is VR's purpose, escalating incidents is a service desk function, and patching vulnerabilities is an IT operations task.

questions.stem: What are some of the recommended duties each SIR team should have?
questions.explanation: All of the above — Coaching, Monitoring activities, and Testing — are recommended duties each SIR team should have. A comprehensive SIR team engages in ongoing skill development (coaching), continuous security event monitoring (monitoring activities), and regular testing of response procedures and tools (testing) to maintain readiness.

questions.stem: Which role is needed to amend Security Incident Response Script Includes?
questions.explanation: The sn_si.admin role is needed to amend Security Incident Response Script Includes. Since SIR is a scoped application, its script includes are protected by the application scope. The sn_si.admin role has full administrative access to all SIR components including script includes. The platform admin role or script_admin cannot directly modify scoped application resources.

questions.stem: Users can create and update security incidents, requests, and tasks, as well as problems, changes, and outages related to their incidents with which role?
questions.explanation: The sn_si.basic role allows users to create and update security incidents, requests, and tasks, as well as problems, changes, and outages related to their incidents. The basic role provides standard operational access for security team members. The itil role is for ITSM, sn_si.manager is for management functions, and sn_si.cisco is not a standard SIR role.

questions.stem: The sn_si.external role is given to external users working on security incidents. What activities can external user complete with this role? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: With the sn_si.external role, external users can View assigned Tasks (C) and Work Tasks assigned to them (D). External users have limited access scoped to only their assigned response tasks — they cannot view the full Security Incident record or related CI records. This restricts sensitive incident details while allowing external contributors to complete their assigned work.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of having an SIR Team? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Benefits of having an SIR Team include: Reduced cost of recovery (A) through efficient response processes, Reduced security incidents (C) through proactive monitoring and prevention, and Dedicated resources (E) ensuring focused security expertise. Increased headcount is a cost, not a benefit. Quicker incident resolutions is a valid benefit but the question asks for three specific options.

questions.stem: What measures activity outputs?
questions.explanation: Lagging indicators measure activity outputs. Lagging indicators track outcomes and results after an activity has completed, such as Mean Time to Contain, number of incidents resolved, and cost per incident. Leading indicators predict future performance, business metrics are broader, and business trends describe directional patterns over time.

questions.stem: Which Security Incident Response product tiers offer baseline orchestration and automation? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Professional and Enterprise tiers of Security Incident Response offer baseline orchestration and automation. Standard and Basic tiers provide core SIR functionality without orchestration capabilities. Professional adds orchestration workflows and Integration Hub access, while Enterprise includes advanced automation features. Orchestration requires the higher tier subscriptions.

questions.stem: What are some of the ways SIR teams can increase their productivity? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: SIR teams can increase productivity through: Process automation (A) to handle repetitive tasks automatically, Form personalization (B) to streamline the analyst interface and reduce clicks, and Training (C) to improve analyst skills and efficiency. Using spreadsheet pivot tables is outside the platform and inefficient, and hiring additional staff increases capacity, not individual productivity.

questions.stem: What roles are required to modify Security Incident Catalog items?
questions.explanation: Both the platform admin role and sn_si.admin role are required to modify Security Incident Catalog items. Catalog items exist at the platform level (requiring admin access for catalog configuration) and within the SIR scope (requiring sn_si.admin for security-specific settings). Neither sn_si.analyst nor sn_si.integration_user have catalog modification permissions.

questions.stem: When designing the Security Incident Catalog what should happen to all catalog items?

options.text: All catalog items should be displayed. These represent incidents common to all businesses.
All catalog items should be designed specifically to that customer's agreed needs.
All catalog items should be removed. They're just examples, and must be replaced by different ones specific to that customer.
All catalog items should be renamed to suit the language for that customer, so users know which to pick.

questions.explanation: When designing the Security Incident Catalog, all catalog items should be designed specifically to that customer's agreed needs. Each organization has different security incident types, terminology, and processes. Catalog items should reflect the customer's actual security operations. Using generic defaults, removing all items, or just renaming items does not properly tailor the catalog to the customer.

questions.stem: Which of the following are required to allow inbound emails to be parsed into Security Incidents? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: To allow inbound emails to be parsed into Security Incidents, you need: Set Properties (A) to configure email processing settings, Set Parsing Rules (B) to define how email content is extracted, and Set Field Transforms (C) to map parsed content to security incident fields. Assignment Rules and Business Rules serve other purposes and are not required specifically for email-to-incident parsing.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are the target personas for MITRE ATT&CK 2.0? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The target personas for MITRE ATT&CK 2.0 are Security and Threat Intelligence Administrators (A), Security Analysis (B) (analysts who use the framework for investigation), and SOC Managers and CISO (D) (leadership who use ATT&CK for strategic planning). IT Project Users are not a target persona for ATT&CK.

questions.stem: Rollup framework capability model configures linked records for what purpose?

options.text: Rollup Data Loss Prevention records to Major Security Incident
Rollup additional records information to Major Security Incident
Rollup additional records information to Data Loss Prevention Incidents
Rollup additional records information to imported Security Incidents

questions.explanation: The Rollup framework capability model configures linked records to rollup additional records information to Major Security Incident. This aggregates data from child security incidents, response tasks, and related records into the Major Security Incident record for consolidated visibility. It does not roll up to DLP records or imported incidents.

questions.stem: Events within the platform that are utilized for the creation of Alerts and/or Security Incidents are held in which table?
questions.explanation: Events utilized for creating Alerts and/or Security Incidents are held in the em_event table. The em_event table is the Event Management event table where all events (including those with Security classification) are stored before processing. The sysevent table stores platform system events (like notifications), not monitoring events. sir_event and sys_event are not the correct tables.

questions.stem: Security Incidents can be created using a manual UI Action on which one of the following record types?
questions.explanation: Security Incidents can be created using a manual UI Action on an Alert record. When an Event Management alert indicates a security concern, analysts can use the 'Create Security Incident' UI action button on the alert form to generate a security incident. Events, Email Notifications, and Workflows do not have this UI action.

questions.stem: Select the one capability that retrieves a list of active network connections from a host or endpoint.
questions.explanation: Get Network Statistics is the capability that retrieves a list of active network connections from a host or endpoint. This integration action queries the endpoint for current network connection information, useful for investigating lateral movement or unauthorized communications. Sightings Search checks observables, Block Action restricts access, Get Running Processes lists processes, and Isolate Host quarantines a device.

questions.stem: LDAP, Direct Web Service, and SOAP are types of what?
questions.explanation: LDAP, Direct Web Service, and SOAP are types of Integration methods. These are protocols and technologies used to integrate ServiceNow with external systems. LDAP integrates with directory services, Direct Web Service makes HTTP calls, and SOAP provides XML-based web service communication. They are not data mapping techniques, access protocols, or reporting methods.

questions.stem: Events received from external tools should include what information? (Choose three.)

options.text: A list of similar indicators that were discovered in the event details
Event description, which populates the description of the security incident
Event classification set to Security to distinguish them from other IT events
Node set to the name, IP address, or sys_id of the CI that becomes the affected resource

questions.explanation: Events from external tools should include: Event description which populates the security incident description (B), Event classification set to Security to distinguish from IT events (C), and Node set to the name, IP address, or sys_id of the CI that becomes the affected resource (E). Lists of similar indicators and whitelisted/blacklisted IPs are not required event fields.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are key features of Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. (Choose three.)

options.text: Perform host enrichment actions to gather more information about the endpoint, which includes host details, logged-in users, and observable related machines details.
Find indicators of compromise (IoC) and enrich security incidents with threat intelligence data.
Perform Enterprise Security Search to sight potential malicious observables across endpoints, and take remediation actions.
Perform response actions such as Isolate host, Remove isolation, Restrict app execution, Run antivirus scan, Remove app restriction, and Stop and quarantine file.

questions.explanation: Key features of Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration include: Perform host enrichment actions to gather endpoint information (A), Find indicators of compromise and enrich incidents with threat intelligence (B), and Perform Enterprise Security Search to sight malicious observables across endpoints with remediation actions (C). These three represent the core enrichment, detection, and response capabilities of the integration.

questions.stem: The time zone of a CI is determined by:

options.text: The time zone setting on the computer
The time zone field on the Clock
The time zone of the asset owner
The time zone of the location

questions.explanation: The time zone of a CI is determined by the time zone of the location. CIs inherit their time zone from their Location record in the CMDB. The Location table has a time zone field that applies to all CIs at that location. Computer time zone settings, clock fields, and asset owner time zones are not used for CI time zone determination in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: Security tags can be applied to which of the following record types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Security tags can be applied to Indicators and observables (C), Response Tasks (D), and Security Incidents (E). Tags like TLP classifications are applied to these security-specific record types to control information sharing and classification. Regular Incidents, Problems, Change Orders, and CMDB CI records do not receive security tags in the SIR context.

questions.stem: The creation of custom process definitions would require which of the following platform components? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Creating custom process definitions requires a Process Definition record (B) to define the states and transitions, and a Script Include (D) to implement the custom logic for state management and validation. Process definitions use script includes to enforce state transition rules. Client-side scripts and Business Rules are not the primary components for process definition creation.

questions.stem: Which Security tag is used when information is useful for the awareness of all participating organizations as well as with peers within the broader community or sector?
questions.explanation: TLP:GREEN is the security tag used when information is useful for awareness of all participating organizations and peers within the broader community or sector. GREEN indicates the information can be shared broadly within the community but not publicly. TLP:RED is most restricted, TLP:AMBER is limited disclosure, and TLP:WHITE is unrestricted public sharing. TLP:PURPLE does not exist.

questions.stem: Which of the following management activities are associated with Major Security Incident Management?

options.text: Link security incidents as child incidents to other child incidents, so that all security incidents can be worked
Link security incidents as parent incidents to the major security incident (MSI) so that all security incidents can be worked
Link security incidents as child incidents to the major security incident (MSI) so that all security incidents can be worked
Link security incidents as minor incidents to the major security incident (MSI) so that all security incidents can be worked

questions.explanation: Major Security Incident Management links security incidents as child incidents to the major security incident (MSI) so that all security incidents can be worked. The parent-child relationship allows the MSI to serve as an umbrella record coordinating response across multiple related security incidents. Child incidents are linked to the MSI (parent), not the other way around.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are key features of Major Security Incident Management. (Choose three.)

options.text: Organize response tasks across multiple parent security incidents
Chat channel manager and activity stream components to manage communications across multiple security, IT, and functional groups via a Microsoft Teams integration
Organize response tasks across multiple 'child' security incidents
Dedicated workspace for managing major security incidents specifically designed for the major security incident manager user role

questions.explanation: Key features of Major Security Incident Management include: Chat channel manager and activity stream for communications via Teams integration (B), Organize response tasks across multiple child security incidents (C), and Dedicated workspace for managing major security incidents for the MSI manager role (D). Organizing tasks across parent incidents (A) is incorrect — tasks are organized across child incidents.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are key features of the Malware Information Sharing Platform. (Choose three.)

options.text: Dedicated workspace for managing major security incidents specifically designed for the major security incident manager user role
Auto-extract MITRE-ATT&CKTM information from MISP attributes and associate the information to SIR security incidents.
Add security incident associated observables as attributes to a MISP event.
Update a MISP event from SIR which includes adding or updating tags, galaxies, or attributes.

questions.explanation: Key features of the Malware Information Sharing Platform (MISP) integration include: Auto-extract MITRE ATT&CK information from MISP attributes and associate to SIR incidents (B), Add security incident observables as attributes to a MISP event (C/E), and Update MISP events from SIR including adding observables (D becomes E conceptually). The dedicated workspace for MSI is a separate feature, not MISP-specific.

questions.stem: Which role must a user have to customize major security incident reports based on the incremental progress since last summary update?
questions.explanation: The sn_msim.workspace_manager role is required to customize major security incident reports based on incremental progress since the last summary update. This role provides management-level access to the MSI workspace including report customization. Note the 'sn_msim' prefix (Major Security Incident Management) rather than 'sn_msi'. The workspace_admin, workspace_user, and sn_msi.workspace_manager are different roles.

questions.stem: Which statement about Security Incident Calculators is correct?

options.text: All Calculator Groups run in order but only the calculator with the highest order in that group runs
All Calculator Groups run in order but only the first matching calculator from each group will apply
All Calculator Groups run in order but only the first matching group will apply
All Calculator Groups run in order and all calculators in the first matching group apply

questions.explanation: All Calculator Groups run in order but only the first matching calculator from each group will apply. Within each calculator group, calculators are evaluated sequentially based on their order field. Once a calculator's conditions match, it is applied and remaining calculators in that group are skipped. The system then moves to the next group. This ensures one calculator per group affects the final score.

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, when an application is identified as a Generic application, which one of the following is the cause?

options.text: No Pattern Identification and Connection Section matches

questions.explanation: In Service Mapping, when no Pattern Identification Section matches for an application, it is identified as a Generic application. The Identification Section contains rules that match specific applications by checking processes, ports, or other attributes. When none of these rules match, the application falls through to the Generic classification as a catch-all. Connection Sections determine relationships between CIs (not identification). Identification Rules are within the pattern (B conflates two sections). The answer is specifically about the Identification Section having no matches.

questions.stem: When a Post-Incident Review report is created, it can be found…

options.text: as a published article in a knowledge base
as an unpublished article in a knowledge base
as an attachment to the original security incident
as an article pending approval in a knowledge base

questions.explanation: When a Post-Incident Review report is created, it can be found as an unpublished article in a knowledge base. The PIR generates a knowledge article draft containing incident details, questionnaire responses, and lessons learned. It is created as unpublished so it can be reviewed and edited before being published or shared. It is not auto-published or saved as an attachment.

questions.stem: What is the main goal of the Security Incident Response process?
questions.explanation: The main goal of the Security Incident Response process is to minimize impact. The ultimate objective of SIR is to reduce the business impact of security incidents through rapid detection, efficient containment, thorough eradication, and quick recovery. Automating processes, reducing time to contain, and saving money are supporting objectives, but minimizing impact is the overarching goal.

questions.stem: What should you consider before helping customers automate different processes?
questions.explanation: Before helping customers automate different processes, you should understand their internal processes. You need to know how security incidents are currently handled before automating anything — automating a broken or undefined process leads to poor outcomes. Understanding existing workflows, handoffs, and decision points ensures automation enhances rather than disrupts operations.

questions.stem: Security Incidents can be created using which platform functionality?
questions.explanation: Security Incidents can be created using Inbound Email Actions. Inbound Email Actions process incoming emails based on conditions and scripts, creating records in target tables including sn_si_incident and sn_si_phishing_email. Email matching rules, Email rules, and Notifications are not the platform functionality that creates records from inbound emails.

questions.stem: Which platform functionality uses Conditions and Scripts to take action on a target table when receiving emails?
questions.explanation: Inbound Email Actions use Conditions and Scripts to take action on a target table when receiving emails. Inbound Email Actions evaluate incoming emails against defined conditions and execute scripts to create or update records in specified target tables. Email Matching Rules, User Reported Phishing Script Include, and Email Scheduler serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Actions packaged in Scoped applications are called:
questions.explanation: Actions packaged in Scoped applications are called Spokes. In the Integration Hub and Flow Designer ecosystem, a spoke is a scoped application containing a collection of related actions, subflows, and integration logic. Spokes provide pre-built integrations with third-party tools. Action Groups, Categories, and Subflows are different concepts within the Flow Designer framework.

questions.stem: When testing a flow, the action outcomes can be found where?
questions.explanation: When testing a flow, the action outcomes can be found in the Execution Details. After a flow test run completes, the Execution Details section shows the results of each action, including input/output values, success/failure status, and any error messages. Configuration Details shows flow setup, System Log has platform events, and Content Record is not a flow testing location.

questions.stem: Flow Logic in the baseline includes: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Flow Logic in the baseline includes For Each Loops (for iterating over collections of records) and If Then conditions (for conditional branching). These two logic constructs enable flows to handle collections and make decisions. Interrupts, Function Calls, and Wait Until are not baseline Flow Logic types (though Wait For is available separately).

questions.stem: What contains a set of reusable operations that are designed to be used in multiple playbooks?
questions.explanation: Subflows contain a set of reusable operations designed to be used in multiple playbooks. Subflows encapsulate common sequences of actions that can be called from different flows, promoting reuse and consistency. Flows are complete automation units with triggers, Actions are individual operations, and Triggers initiate flows — none are specifically designed for cross-playbook reuse.

questions.stem: What automates processes and supports triggers with a sequence of reusable actions?
questions.explanation: Flows automate processes and support triggers with a sequence of reusable actions. A flow is the primary automation construct in Flow Designer, consisting of a trigger that starts it and a sequence of actions that execute. Subflows are reusable components without triggers, Actions are individual steps, and Activities is legacy workflow terminology.

questions.stem: Once a Phishing Email record is created, which Flow creates a new Security Incident record?

options.text: Transform Phishing Email to Security Incident

questions.explanation: Once a Phishing Email record is created, the Transform Phishing Email to Security Incident flow creates a new Security Incident record. This flow processes the phishing email record, extracts relevant information, and generates a security incident with pre-populated fields. The Automated Phishing Playbook runs after the incident exists, and the other options are not valid flow names.

questions.stem: When an inbound email is processed and identified as a phishing email what table is it stored in for URP v2?
questions.explanation: When an inbound email identified as phishing is processed for URP v2, it is stored in the Security Incident Phishing Email table (sn_si_phishing_email). This specialized table captures phishing-specific details including headers, observables, and email content before a security incident is created. The record is not stored directly in the Security Incident or Incident tables.

questions.stem: In order to use User Reported Phishing v2, what must occur in Flow Designer?

options.text: Phishing Email Aggregation Subflow must be activated
Transform Flow must be copied and activated

questions.explanation: To use User Reported Phishing v2, the Transform Flow must be activated in Flow Designer. The transform flow is responsible for converting phishing email records into security incidents. It comes deactivated by default and must be explicitly activated to enable the URP v2 processing pipeline. Publishing, copying, or activating actions/subflows is not the correct step.

questions.stem: When setting up a Playbook what field in the Flow Action for Creating a Response Task must contain the same value as the Runbook name?
questions.explanation: When setting up a Playbook, the Runbook field in the Flow Action for Creating a Response Task must contain the same value as the Runbook name. This creates the link between the flow's response task and the runbook containing guidance knowledge articles. If the Runbook field value does not match an existing runbook name, the task will not have associated documentation.

questions.stem: Runbook records utilize a link to what type record for content?
questions.explanation: Runbook records utilize a link to a Knowledge article for content. Runbooks connect response tasks to knowledge base articles that contain step-by-step instructions for analysts. The knowledge article provides the actual procedural content, while the runbook record creates the linkage. Response Tasks, Managed Documents, and Instruction Details are not the content source for runbooks.

questions.stem: In a Flow, if the Create Response Task set Incident state V1 action is selected, what field contains the yes_no value that drives a question being asked in the playbook?
questions.explanation: The Outcome Type field contains the yes_no value that drives a question being asked in the playbook. When the Create Response Task set Incident state V1 action's Outcome Type is set to yes_no, the playbook presents the analyst with a yes/no decision point that determines the flow's branching path. Question Type, SI State, and Answer Type are not the correct fields.

questions.stem: Runbooks are used to create a relationship between what components? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Runbooks create a relationship between Playbook Tasks (C) and Knowledge articles (F). The runbook links a specific playbook response task to a knowledge article containing procedural guidance. This association ensures analysts have documented instructions available when working each task. Events, Alerts, and Workflow Triggers are not directly linked through runbooks.

questions.stem: What is included in the real-time data model in the right pane of the Flow Designer UI that may be dragged and dropped into fields in the main flow workspace?
questions.explanation: Data Pills are included in the real-time data model in the right pane of the Flow Designer UI and can be dragged and dropped into fields. Data pills represent available data values from trigger records, action outputs, and flow variables. They provide a visual, code-free way to reference data within flow actions. Record Objects, Table References, and Code Snippets are not the correct term.

questions.stem: What kind of rules can be used to configure how email phishing incidents are processed? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Ingestion Rules and Duplication Rules can be used to configure how email phishing incidents are processed. Ingestion rules determine how phishing emails are evaluated and promoted to security incidents. Duplication rules check whether a phishing email has already been reported to prevent duplicate incidents. Risk Rules, Inbound Property Rules, CI Lookup Rules, and Condition Rules are not used for phishing email processing.

questions.stem: Which role must a user have to customize major security incident reports based on the incremental progress since last summary update?
questions.explanation: The sn_msi.workspace_manager role is required to customize major security incident reports based on incremental progress since the last summary update. This role grants management-level access to the MSI workspace including the ability to customize and generate progress reports. The workspace_user and workspace_responder roles have insufficient permissions for report customization.

questions.stem: Risk Score weighting uses which of the following components? (Choose two.)

options.text: Business impact of a CI or Security Incident
Severity and Priority of a Security incident
Cost and Risk of an affected service
SLA and Schedule of an impacted service
Impact and Urgency of a Security incident

questions.explanation: Risk Score weighting uses Business impact of a CI or Security Incident (A) and Impact and Urgency of a Security incident (E). The risk score calculation considers the business criticality of affected assets and the standard ITSM impact/urgency values. Severity and Priority are derived values, Cost and Risk are not direct weighting components, and SLA/Schedule are not part of risk scoring.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for identifying security incidents?
questions.explanation: Everyone is responsible for identifying security incidents. Security awareness is an organization-wide responsibility — any employee who notices suspicious activity, phishing emails, or unusual system behavior should report it. While security analysts investigate and respond, the initial identification of potential security incidents is not limited to IT personnel, managers, or security specialists.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are key features of the Malware Information Sharing Platform (Choose three.)

options.text: Dedicated MISP workspace for managing major security incidents
Auto-extract MITRE-ATT&CK™ information from MISP attributes and associate them to SIR security incidents
Attribute enrichment including adding or updating tags, galaxies, or attributes
Send malware to MISP for detonation
Add security incident associated observables as attributes to a MISP event

questions.explanation: Key features of MISP integration include: Auto-extract MITRE ATT&CK information from MISP attributes and associate them to SIR security incidents (B), Attribute enrichment including adding or updating tags, galaxies, or attributes (C), and Add security incident associated observables as attributes to a MISP event (E). Dedicated MISP workspace and malware detonation are not MISP integration features.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are the target personas for MITRE ATT&CK 2.0? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The target personas for MITRE ATT&CK 2.0 are SOC Managers and CISO (A), Security and Threat Intelligence Administrators (B), and Security Analysts (C). These three personas use the ATT&CK framework for strategic planning, threat intelligence management, and tactical investigation respectively. Compliance Managers and Penetration Testers are not primary ATT&CK 2.0 target personas.

questions.stem: How does a user modify Risk Scores to suit their organizational needs?

options.text: alter values in the Risk Score Configuration module
amend constants in the RiskScoreUtil script include
change the business impact for affected Business Services and Configuration Items
recode logic in the Risk Score Calculator

questions.explanation: To modify Risk Scores to suit organizational needs, you amend constants in the RiskScoreUtil script include. The RiskScoreUtil script include contains the calculation logic and weighting constants used in risk score computation. By modifying these constants, administrators can adjust how different factors contribute to the final risk score. The Risk Score Configuration module and Risk Score Calculator are not the correct modification points.

questions.stem:
Universal Containers (UC) is preparing for the new Salesforce release in a couple of months, and has several ongoing development projects that may be affected.
Which three steps should the team at UC take to prepare for this release? (Choose three.)

options.text: Upgrade any SOAP integrations to the newest WSDL as early as possible.
Contact Salesforce to schedule a time to upgrade the Full sandbox.
Review the release notes for automatically-enabled features and technical debt.
Refresh a Sandbox during the Release Preview Window to ensure they have the upcoming release.
Run regression tests in an upgraded sandbox to detect any issues with the upgrade.

questions.explanation: To prepare for a new Salesforce release: (C) Review release notes for automatically-enabled features and any technical debt that needs addressing. (D) Refresh a sandbox during the Release Preview Window to get the upcoming release for testing. (E) Run regression tests in the upgraded sandbox to detect compatibility issues. Upgrading SOAP integrations early (A) is premature since the release hasn't arrived. Contacting Salesforce to schedule sandbox upgrades (B) is not necessary as sandbox refreshes follow the preview schedule automatically.

questions.stem: What are some of the ways SIR teams can increase their productivity? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: SIR teams can increase productivity through: Process automation (A) to handle repetitive tasks, Training (C) to improve analyst capabilities and efficiency, and Form personalization (D) to streamline workflows and reduce unnecessary clicks. Red/Blue automation and exporting to spreadsheet pivot tables are not standard SIR productivity methods. This question is similar to Q71 with slightly different option ordering.

questions.stem: What is one of the Security Incident Response Team’s activities?
questions.explanation: Monitoring security alerts is one of the Security Incident Response Team's activities. The SIR team actively monitors alerts from security tools and event management systems to detect potential security incidents. Patching vulnerabilities is an IT operations task, escalating incidents is a service desk function, and penetration testing is performed by dedicated security assessment teams.

questions.stem:
Universal Containers (UC) is about to begin development work on a new project in their Salesforce org that will take many months to complete. UC is concerned about how critical bugs will be addressed for existing live functionality.
What is the recommended release management strategy to address this concern?

options.text: Include fixes for critical bugs in the ongoing Development sandboxes so that they will be released with the other code.
Keep teams separate until the end of the project and create a Full Copy sandbox to merge their work then.
Utilize a dedicated developer pro sandbox to address critical bugs and release to production.
Address critical bugs in the Development sandboxes and push those changes to production separately.

questions.explanation: For addressing critical bugs while a long development project is ongoing, the recommended strategy is to use a dedicated Developer Pro sandbox specifically for critical bug fixes. This keeps bug fix work separate from the main development project, allowing critical fixes to be tested and deployed to production independently without waiting for the larger project to complete. Mixing fixes into Development sandboxes (A/D) risks incomplete code reaching production. A Full Copy merge at project end (B) delays critical fixes.
